title: Rabbi Yehudah bar Chanina
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman identifies him as Resh Lakish’s teacher, citing [Eruvin](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.11a.19) without a folio: Resh Lakish spoke in his name, and they answered, “There is no difficulty: one is his own view, the other his teacher’s.”

In [Ketubot 49b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.49b.4), [Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 4:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Ketubot.4.8.3), and at the beginning of [Peah, chapter 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Peah.1.1.12), Resh Lakish gives several teachings in his name.
Hyman cites [Bava Kamma 8:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Bava_Kamma.8.6.2): a man insulted R’ Yehudah bar Chanina, and Resh Lakish fined him a litra of gold.

Hyman also cites Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 5:4 (compare [5:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Terumot.5.2.2)) for a teaching R’ Acha gives in his name. Hyman gives the reading “R’ Yudah bei Levi” for the parallel in [Sukkah 2:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sukkah.2.8.3).

Hyman cites Ruth Rabbah 2:15 (compare [2:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Ruth_Rabbah.2.16)) for R’ Shmuel B-N [ב״נ] speaking in his name, and Midrash Tehillim 3:4 (compare [3:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tehillim.3.3)) for another mention of Yehudah bar Chanina.[^4]

notes.text: The abbreviation ב״נ after Shmuel remains unresolved. Hyman’s Yehudah bar Chanina / Yudah bei Levi readings remain distinct; the teacher and insult traditions are his cited accounts.

No new primary scalar was returned. The heading explicitly writes full Rabbi; uninspected abbreviated body titles remain R-prime. Hyman’s teacher inference and gold-fine story are attributed to him, preserving who insulted whom and who imposed the fine. Eruvin has no supplied folio. Peah is BEGINNING CHAPTER1. Yehudah bar Chanina and Yudah bei Levi remain distinct readings. Shmuel ב״נ remains unresolved; an earlier finite Ruth2:15 miss and phrase-search miss are not global absence or proof of bar Nachman.

The consulted Eruvin 11a–b names Yehudah be-Rabbi Chanina in Resh Lakish’s chain before distinguishing Resh Lakish’s view from his teacher’s. The teaching Hyman cites from Terumot 5:4 appears at Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 5:2 in the consulted edition, with both R’ Chizkiyah and R’ Acha named. The parallel at Sukkah 2:8 reads Yudah ben Levi. In the consulted Ruth Rabbah 2:16, R’ Shmuel bar Nachmani reports the teaching about approaching a prospective convert in the name of R’ Yudan be-Rabbi Chanina. Hyman gives 2:15 and abbreviates Shmuel’s patronymic. The consulted Midrash Tehillim chapter 3, paragraph 3 names R’ Yehudah bar Chanina in the David homily. Hyman’s older numbering remains as supplied.

[Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1669&lang=en) also connects the teacher inference to Eruvin. The distinction between Resh Lakish’s own view and his teacher’s follows on [11b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.11b.2). In the two Yerushalmi accounts of which school conceded, both Chizkiyah and Acha transmit the teaching. Terumot names Yudah bar Chanina and Sukkah names Yudah ben Levi. The consulted Ruth Rabbah spells out Shmuel bar Nachmani.
